sources.entry: Aeron - Carries the single writer and batching rules through a whole transport, the reference beyond one in-process queue.

summary.one_liner: Aeron is a high-performance messaging transport for reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, and IPC messaging, with Java, C, C++, and .NET clients.
summary.what_it_does: Aeron moves messages between processes over reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, or IPC on a single machine. The README names Java, C, and C++ clients in this repository, plus a .NET client. Message streams can be recorded by the Archive module to persistent storage for later or real-time replay. Aeron Cluster provides fault-tolerant services as replicated state machines based on the Raft consensus algorithm. The project states that performance, meaning highest throughput with low and predictable latency, is its main design focus. It integrates with Simple Binary Encoding (SBE) for message encoding and uses data structures factored out into the Agrona project.
how_to_run: Java programming guide, C++11 programming guide, and Building Aeron pages are linked from the README wiki; no install commands appear in the README itself
notable: Single transport covering unicast, multicast, and IPC messaging
Aeron Archive records streams for persistent storage and replay
Aeron Cluster offers Raft-based replicated state machines
Designed around throughput and predictable latency as primary goals
caveats: README mentions paid Aeron Premium offerings, including proprietary enhancements such as DPDK kernel bypass and ATS encryption
Detailed usage, protocol, and build instructions are on the external wiki rather than in the README
